theater: 查科北部與上巴拉圭河

battle.name: 查科戰爭
battle.theater: 查科北部與上巴拉圭河
battle.brief: 一九三二年六月起，玻利維亞與巴拉圭為爭奪內陸查科盆地而開火，戰事延續三年，雙方先後投入數十萬人與大批飛機，卡面的英製維克斯.303水冷式機槍是巴拉圭軍在木柵堡壘中壓制森林射界的骨幹火力，卻也最怕查科沙塵卡死機匣。整場戰爭的勝負，始終由糧秣能否運到前線決定。

kit.name: 維克斯.303水冷式機槍
kit.history: 作為英國軍的標準中型機槍，維克斯.303在一次大戰與後續衝突中被廣泛使用，以其水冷式結構提供持續火力支援，成為步兵與火力支援的主力裝備。

countries: 交戰的兩方是南美洲兩個內陸國家。巴拉圭軍隊由法國軍事顧問團協助整建，參戰規模在開戰初期極小，一九三二年六月全軍僅約四千零二十六人，另有見習生二百人、士官六百九十人、軍醫與非作戰軍官一百四十六人；到戰爭後期，該國以全民總動員的方式擴軍，徵召年齡下限一再下調，連公務警察都編入部隊，壯丁幾乎全部被送上前線。玻利維亞軍隊則由德國軍事顧問團整建，總參謀長是德國人漢斯·孔特，指揮官多出自德國教練系統；步兵主力是來自高原的克丘亞與艾馬拉徵召農民，基層與士官之間存在明顯的種族落差，士兵慣於三千七百公尺的高原生活，初到低窪炎熱的查科平原極不適應。玻利維亞的總人數與裝備規模遠勝巴拉圭，最多動員過六萬人，且有三分之二兵力被送上查科戰線，卻因鐵路不進戰區、公路稀疏而難以把補給送到前線。巴拉圭的陸軍是絕對主力，海軍則以內河炮艇與汽船沿巴拉圭河輸送部隊；玻利維亞也組織了十餘艘自製巡邏艇與運輸船，在馬莫雷—馬德拉河水系與帕拉圭河上游活動。英、美、義等國以觀察員、顧問與工程技術人員的形式介入，試圖在不正式參戰的前提下影響戰局走向。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were two landlocked South American republics. The Paraguayan army had been organised with the help of a French military mission, and its size at the opening of hostilities was tiny: in June 1932 the whole army numbered about 4,026 men, together with 200 cadets, 690 non-commissioned officers and 146 surgeons and non-combat officers. By the later stages of the war the country expanded the army by a total mobilisation, repeatedly lowering the age of conscription and even folding the police into the ranks, so that practically the whole body of able-bodied men was sent to the front. The Bolivian army, by contrast, had been reorganised by a German military mission under a German chief of staff, Hans Kundt, and most of its officers came out of the German training system. The bulk of its infantry were Quechua and Aymara conscripts drawn from the highlands, with a pronounced ethnic gap between the rank and file and the officer corps; used to life at 3,700 metres above sea level, the men found the low, sweltering Chaco plain profoundly hard to bear. Bolivia possessed far greater manpower and far better equipment than Paraguay, mobilising at most 60,000 men and putting two thirds of them into the Chaco, yet it struggled to deliver supplies to the front because no railway reached the theatre and the roads were poor. For Paraguay the army was the decisive arm, while its navy moved troops by river gunboats and steamers along the Paraguay River; Bolivia likewise put at least ten locally built patrol boats and transport vessels to work on the Mamoré-Madeira system and the upper Paraguay. Britain, the United States and Italy intervened in the form of observers, advisers and engineering technicians, seeking to shape the course of the war without formally entering it.
people: 巴拉圭方面，戰爭為這個國家造就了兩位現代軍史上的代表人物。戰爭初期任軍團長、其後升任全軍最高指揮官的何塞·費利克斯·埃斯蒂加里比亞，善用瓜拉尼語住民的森林知識與就地取糧能力，主張以快速行軍和迂迴包抄對付玻利維亞的正面陣地，他本人長期在林區指揮，屢次脫離險境；其屬下上校拉斐爾·弗朗科擅長滲透與包圍作戰。戰事結束時，巴拉圭方面扣押的玻利維亞俘虜逾兩萬一千人，玻利維亞方面則僅約二千五百人，這組數字直接反映了包圍滲透戰法的效果。參謀長埃米利奧·道恩等人主持了軍需生產、鐵路運輸與前線補給體系。玻利維亞方面，總統丹尼爾·薩拉曼卡在皮蒂安圖塔事件後放棄對查科哨所的克制政策，下令奪取科拉萊斯、托萊多與布克耶隆；將軍菲利貝爾托·奧索里奧曾遞交以北方進攻為核心的作戰計畫；德國籍總參謀長漢斯·孔特主持擴軍與引進坦克部隊，卻因戰局失利與下屬不滿於一九三三年被撤換，由恩里克·佩納蘭達接掌全軍，日後格爾曼·布希也在前線師級指揮崗位上嶄露頭角，兩人後來都登上玻利維亞總統之位。戰地另一類重要人物是雙方的空軍飛行員、工兵與技術顧問：美方軍事觀察團的教官與工程人員幾乎全程參與了巴拉圭查科公路的修建，玻利維亞方面則有德國顧問主持飛機維修與空投作業。
peopleEn: On the Paraguayan side the war produced the two leading figures of that country's modern military history. José Félix Estigarribia, who commanded a corps at the start of the fighting and later rose to command the entire army, drew on the forest knowledge and the ability to live off the land of the Guaraní inhabitants, and insisted on rapid marches and turning movements against the Bolivian frontal positions; he spent much of the war commanding inside the forest and narrowly escaped destruction more than once. His subordinate, Colonel Rafael Franco, proved adept at infiltration and encirclement. When the fighting ended Paraguay held more than 21,000 Bolivian prisoners of war against roughly 2,500 held by Bolivia, a ratio that directly measures the effect of the encirclement and infiltration style of war. General Emilio Dawn and his colleagues ran the war economy, the railway transport and the forward supply system. On the Bolivian side, President Daniel Salamanca abandoned his policy of restraint towards the Chaco outposts after the Pitiantutá incident and ordered the capture of Corrales, Toledo and Boquerón. General Filiberto Osorio submitted a plan of operations built around a northern offensive. The German chief of staff, Hans Kundt, presided over the expansion of the army and the acquisition of tanks, but he was removed in 1933 after defeats and the resentment of his subordinates, and command of the whole army passed to Enrique Peñaranda; Germán Busch also made his name commanding a division in the line, and both men would later sit in the presidential palace of Bolivia. A second category of important participants were the airmen, engineers and technical advisers on both sides: instructors and engineers of the American military observer mission took part almost throughout in building the Paraguayan Chaco road, while German advisers in Bolivia ran aircraft maintenance and the aerial supply system.
kits: 卡面這件英製維克斯.303水冷式機槍，是查科戰場上巴拉圭軍的骨幹火力。開戰之初，巴拉圭步兵手中的輕武器五花八門：德製馬克西姆機槍、英製維克斯、勃朗寧M1938水冷式機槍與丹麥製麥德森輕機槍混雜並行，制式步槍則是以阿根廷M1909長槍為底、由西班牙奧維耶多兵工廠仿製的M1927式7.65毫米長槍，此槍連射容易過熱，槍機偶爾斷裂，後來經查獲的玻利維亞VZ-24步槍與MP28衝鋒鎗才勉強補上前線步兵的火力缺口。維克斯.303的長處正在水套帶來的高溫容限：槍手能在灌木與林莽之間以低射界長時間壓制對方步槍手，配合木柵陣地與交錯射界構成堡壘防線的核心，而巴拉圭人少彈少，正是靠這種射速慢卻不必換槍的機槍維持火力密度。戰地環境卻是它最大的敵人，查科平原乾旱多塵，數以千計的車輛與水冷式機槍的機匣被沙塵卡死，缺水時水套又成了額外拖累。玻利維亞方面的機槍以德製DWM馬克西姆M1904與M1911、捷克ZB vz.26輕機槍和Vickers-Berthier為主；火炮兩造懸殊，玻利維亞有德造牽引砲與一九三二年十二月入役的維克斯A型、B型輕戰車，巴拉圭則大量採購英國Stokes-Brandt M1931迫擊砲，射程約三千碼，當地以瓜拉尼語angu'as稱之，另有自製手投炸藥carumbe'i，意為小烏龜。摩托化與航空同樣關鍵：玻利維亞以四架容克Ju 52執行醫療後送與空投，向前線運送逾四千四百噸物資；巴拉圭以十四架Potez 25雙翼機與後購的Travel Air六千型執行同樣任務，義製Macchi M.18水上機則從巴伊亞內格拉基地出動。雙方雖都保留騎兵團，卻因查科缺水缺草而幾乎全數改作步兵，僅少量擔任師級偵察。
kitsEn: The British Vickers .303 water-cooled machine gun on the card was the backbone of Paraguayan firepower in the Chaco. At the outset the light weapons in Paraguayan infantry hands were a motley collection: German Maxim machine guns, British Vickers, Browning M1938 water-cooled guns and Danish Madsen light machine guns were all mixed together, while the service rifle was the M1927 7.65 mm long rifle, a Mauser design based on the Argentine M1909 and copied by the Oviedo arsenal in Spain; it overheated on rapid fire and its receiver occasionally cracked, and only captured Bolivian VZ-24 rifles and MP28 submachine guns, nicknamed piripipi, later plugged the gap in the front-line infantry's firepower. The strength of the Vickers .303 lay in the heat tolerance its water jacket provided: a gunner could hold a low line of sight through scrub and woodland and suppress enemy riflemen for long stretches, and in combination with wooden stockades and interlocking fields of fire it formed the core of the fortification system. Paraguay, short of men and short of ammunition, leaned on exactly this kind of weapon that fired slowly but did not need changing. The battlefield, however, was its greatest enemy: the Chaco plain is arid and dusty, and thousands of vehicles and the receivers of water-cooled machine guns were jammed with sand, while in the absence of water the jacket became a burden in its own right. Bolivia's machine guns were mainly German DWM Maxim M1904 and M1911, Czech ZB vz.26 light guns and Vickers-Berthier. The gap in artillery was wide: Bolivia had German towed guns and Vickers Type A and Type B light tanks, commissioned in December 1932, while Paraguay bought large quantities of the British Stokes-Brandt Model 1931 mortar, accurate over roughly 3,000 yards and called angu'as, corn-mashers, in Guaraní, and produced its own pineapple-shaped hand grenade, the carumbe'i, little turtle. Motorisation and aviation mattered as much: Bolivia used four Junkers Ju 52 for medical evacuation and aerial supply, delivering more than 4,400 tons of cargo to the front, while Paraguay flew fourteen Potez 25 biplanes and later Travel Air 6000 transports on the same work, with Italian-built Macchi M.18 flying boats operating from the Bahía Negra base. Both armies kept cavalry regiments, but since the dry Chaco could not support horses with water and forage they were almost entirely converted to infantry, with only a few squadrons left for divisional reconnaissance.
tactics: 巴拉圭的戰法核心是速度、迂迴與滲透。埃斯蒂加里比亞不正面強攻，而是依托自修的窄軌鐵路與公路，把部隊以小縱隊快速推入查科森林，藉助當地嚮導繞過玻利維亞的堡壘，以散兵包圍、封鎖退路，最後迫使守軍繳械；一九三二年九月強攻布克耶隆堡壘時，約五千人的巴拉圭部隊圍困守軍六百一十九人達二十二天，兩千五百名玻利維亞人出擊解圍亦未成功，正是這種圍而不急攻、斷其補給做法的典型。玻利維亞則回到更正規的作戰方式，靠北向正面推進、逐個奪取哨所，試圖以正面火力壓制對手，同時倚重德國顧問建立縱深梯隊與預備隊制度。雙方都大量使用塹壕與木柵堡壘，架設鐵絲網、地雷、迫擊砲與機槍構成交錯射界，並在關鍵道路設置路障與雷區；日間作戰與夜間襲擊併用，巴拉圭常以小分隊滲透破壞對方交通線與補給點，玻利維亞則倚重空中偵察與轟炸，卻屢屢不採納前線觀察員報告的包圍警告，其中一次是偵察發現巴拉圭迂迴部隊已插向側翼，總參謀部仍斥為飛行員誇大其詞。通信與後勤是決定性環節：巴拉圭以瓜拉尼語進行無線電通話，而多數玻利維亞士兵不懂這種語言，截獲與誤讀的風險集中在一方；巴拉圭有五條窄軌鐵路共約四百二十八公里直達查科前線，火車把補給從巴拉圭河口岸卡薩多港直接送到最前沿，玻利維亞的物資卻要從三千七百公尺高原下到一百五十公尺的查科，士兵步行需十四天，車輛每日行程短、故障率高。
tacticsEn: The core of the Paraguayan method was speed, turning movements and infiltration. Estigarribia avoided frontal assault and instead pushed small columns into the Chaco forest along his own narrow-gauge railway and roads, using local guides to bypass Bolivian strongpoints, surrounding them with scattered parties, sealing their escape route and finally compelling the garrisons to surrender. In the assault on Fortín Boquerón in September 1932 a Paraguayan force of about 5,000 men besieged 619 defenders for twenty-two days, and a Bolivian relief attempt by some 2,500 men failed; this was the classic expression of besieging without hurry and cutting the supply route. Bolivia reverted to a more conventional approach, pushing north in frontal movement and seizing outpost by outpost, trying to overwhelm the enemy with frontal fire while relying on the German mission to build a system of echeloned formations and reserve troops. Both sides dug in heavily, using trenches and wooden stockades, and strung barbed wire, mines, mortars and machine guns into interlocking fields of fire, with roadblocks and minefields on the key routes. They fought by day and raided by night; Paraguay habitually sent small parties to infiltrate and wreck the enemy's lines of communication and supply points, while Bolivia relied on aerial reconnaissance and bombardment yet repeatedly ignored the warnings of its own forward observers, on one occasion dismissing as pilot exaggeration the sighting of a Paraguayan flanking force already driving in on the side. Communications and logistics were decisive: Paraguay spoke in Guaraní over the radio while most Bolivian soldiers did not understand the language, so the risk of interception and confusion fell heavily on one side; Paraguay ran five narrow-gauge lines totalling some 428 kilometres straight to the Chaco front, with trains carrying supplies from the river port of Puerto Casado to the forwardmost positions, whereas Bolivia's supplies had to descend from 3,700-metre highlands to a Chaco only 150 metres above sea level, a soldier taking fourteen days on foot, with vehicle convoys covering short daily distances and breaking down often.
data: 一九三二年六月，巴拉圭陸軍總兵力約四千零二十六人，其中作戰軍官三百五十五人、軍醫與非作戰軍官一百四十六人、見習生二百人、士官六百九十人、士兵二千六百五十三人。玻利維亞在衝突區的第一軍約四千人，八月再增援六千人，最終全國動員不超過六萬人，其中在查科作戰者約佔三分之二。巴拉圭的查科鐵路系統由五條窄軌線組成，總長約四百二十八公里；玻利維亞的公路網極差，前線距離其高原後方約八百公里，士兵步行需十四天，而巴拉圭士兵只需四天。玻利維亞四架Ju 52運載機向前線投送逾四千四百噸物資，空軍方面至少出動二十架CW-14魚鷹雙翼機，巴拉圭出動十四架Potez 25。布克耶隆堡壘守軍六百一十九人，被約五千人的巴拉圭部隊圍困二十二天。戰爭結束時巴拉圭方面扣押玻利維亞俘虜逾兩萬一千人，玻利維亞方面約二千五百人。人口對比是另一組數字：玻利維亞約二百一十五萬人，巴拉圭約八十八萬人；當時廣為流傳的概略說法是戰爭造成的死亡約相當於玻利維亞人口的百分之二、巴拉圭人口的百分之三。玻利維亞於一九三二年十二月接收維克斯A型與B型輕戰車，另有十餘艘自製巡邏艇投入馬莫雷—馬德拉河水系。傷亡的精確數字各方記載互相矛盾，較可靠的說法是雙方各有數千人陣亡，因疾病、飢渴與麻痺造成的非戰傷減員遠多於戰鬥傷亡；一九三四年十二月的皮賴戰役中，巴拉圭深入玻利維亞境內二百餘公里，一度直逼聖克魯斯城。
dataEn: In June 1932 the Paraguayan army numbered about 4,026 men in total, of whom 355 were combat officers, 146 surgeons and non-combat officers, 200 were cadets, 690 were non-commissioned officers and 2,653 were privates. Bolivia's First Army in the conflict zone numbered some 4,000 men, was reinforced in August with 6,000 more, and the country never mobilised more than 60,000 men in total, of whom roughly two thirds served in the Chaco. Paraguay's Chaco railway system consisted of five narrow-gauge lines totalling about 428 kilometres; Bolivia's road network was poor, the front lay some 800 kilometres from its highland rear areas, and it took a Bolivian soldier fourteen days to march that distance against four for a Paraguayan. Bolivia's four Ju 52 transports dropped more than 4,400 tons of cargo at the front, and its air arm flew at least twenty CW-14 Osprey biplanes against the fourteen Potez 25 of Paraguay. The garrison of Fortín Boquerón, 619 men, was besieged for twenty-two days by a Paraguayan force of roughly 5,000. When the war ended Paraguay held more than 21,000 Bolivian prisoners of war against about 2,500 held by Bolivia. Population provides another set of figures: Bolivia had roughly 2,150,000 people and Paraguay about 880,000, and the estimate then current in circulation was that the war killed the equivalent of about two per cent of the Bolivian population and three per cent of the Paraguayan. Bolivia commissioned Vickers Type A and Type B light tanks in December 1932 and committed more than ten locally built patrol boats to the Mamoré-Madeira water system. Exact casualty figures conflict between the various accounts; the more reliable statement is that each side lost several thousand men in action, while non-battle losses from disease, thirst and dysentery far exceeded battle casualties. In the Battle of Piraí in December 1934 the Paraguayan advance drove more than 200 kilometres into Bolivian territory and came within sight of the city of Santa Cruz.
cause: 戰爭的根源是土地、河流與石油三條線索交匯。玻利維亞在一八七九年太平洋戰爭中失去太平洋沿岸，此後又在所謂的東北戰爭中被自家軍隊捲入查科內部的武裝衝突；而一九二九年的利馬條約正式堵死了玻利維亞經秘魯重返太平洋的可能，於是經由巴拉圭河通往大西洋的通道成了國家經濟的生死線。查科地區約六十萬平方公里，牧樹林與養牛業早已被巴拉圭與阿根廷的牧戶分割，一九一九年前後阿根廷的銀行已持有東部查科約四十萬公頃地產，阿根廷寡頭卡西多家族亦有約十四萬一千公頃；當地聚居的瓜拉尼語原住民與巴拉圭同族，玻利維亞在國際仲裁上則援引原西班牙莫克索斯與奇基托斯省的主權繼承權。邊界從未真正劃定，一九二五年成立的混合邊界委員會因談判破裂而無疾而終，衝突逐步升級：一九二七年玻利維亞的驚奇堡拘禁並槍斃巴拉圭中尉羅哈斯·席爾瓦，一九二八年十二月五日巴拉圭攻陷玻利維亞先鋒堡，十二月二十四日玻利維亞反攻攻下布克耶隆堡壘並擊斃十五名巴方人員，一九二九年九月在華盛頓經美洲聯盟施壓才回到戰前狀態，但武器競賽已悄然展開。石油是最後一根引線：安第斯山東麓發現油氣後，標準石油與殼牌分別支持玻利維亞與巴拉圭，阿根廷也希望自查科進口石油；史家 Matthew Hughes 則認為公司與政府檔案中的硬證據薄弱，反駁了兩國只是石油公司傀儡的說法。真正引爆戰爭的是軍人的地盤意識與國家的生存焦慮：巴拉圭在同治戰爭失利後失去了大片領土，一旦控制查科與河段即可確保航運與經濟命脈。
causeEn: The roots of the war lie in the convergence of land, river and oil. Bolivia had lost its Pacific coast in the War of the Pacific in 1879 and was then drawn into armed conflict inside the Chaco through its own army during the so-called Northeastern War; the 1929 Treaty of Lima closed off for good the hope of regaining the Pacific through Peru, so that access to the Atlantic by way of the Paraguay River became a matter of national economic survival. The Chaco covered about 600,000 square kilometres, and its quebracho timber and cattle ranches had long been divided between Paraguayan and Argentine ranchers; by about 1919 Argentine banks already held about 400,000 hectares in the eastern Chaco, and the Casado family, a pillar of the Argentine oligarchy, held 141,000. The nomadic Guaraní-speaking inhabitants of the region were kin to Paraguay's own people, while Bolivia's case in international arbitration rested on succession to the former Spanish provinces of Moxos and Chiquitos. The border was never truly delimited, and the mixed boundary commission set up in 1925 collapsed without agreement as the clashes escalated: in 1927 Bolivian troops at Fortín Sorpresa took a Paraguayan patrol prisoner and shot Lieutenant Adolfo Rojas Silva; on 5 December 1928 the Paraguayans overran Fortín Vanguardia; on 14 December Bolivia counter-attacked, taking Fortín Boquerón and killing fifteen Paraguayans; and only in September 1929, in Washington, under pressure from the Pan-American League, was the status quo ante bellum restored, though the arms race had already begun. Oil was the last straw: after petroleum was found in the eastern Andean foothills, Standard Oil backed Bolivia and Royal Dutch Shell backed Paraguay, and Argentina wanted to import oil from the Chaco as well, though the historian Matthew Hughes argued from the company and government archives that the hard evidence for the theory that the two governments were mere puppets of the oil companies was thin. What actually lit the fuse was the territorial instinct of the generals and the existential anxiety of the states: Paraguay had lost vast territories after the War of the Triple Alliance, and control of the Chaco and the river would guarantee its navigation and its economic lifeline.
impact: 這場戰爭是南美洲二十世紀最血腥的衝突之一，卻也把現代戰爭形態完整地帶進了熱帶內陸：重機槍、輕戰車、牽引砲、迫擊砲與航空兵同時投入大規模消耗，成為美洲第一場大規模使用現代武器的戰爭，也是第一場大規模航空戰。技術層面的遺產最為深遠，空投補給、以空中偵察引導包圍、由公路與窄軌鐵路支撐的機動作戰，以及以木柵堡壘與交錯射界構成的防禦體系，都在此得到驗證並被後來的歐洲戰爭借鑑；英、美、義等國以觀察員、顧問與工程技術的形式介入，也開啟了大國在區域衝突中不正式參戰而施加影響的先例。政治上，玻利維亞在戰前已爆發反對派武裝起義，軍隊在查科對付武裝分子時越界作戰，士氣與輿論都受牽連；戰後改革派推倒長期把持政權的寡頭統治，軍方在政治上的分量隨之急升，數年後軍人索性直接奪權。巴拉圭則以勝利鞏固了威權體制，埃斯蒂加里比亞其後出任總統，推行國家改革，最終在一九四○年遇刺身亡。長期看，查科在兩次大戰之間始終是未經仲裁的空白，一九三八年的最終條約才劃定永久邊界。經濟上，玻利維亞終於在查科探得並開採石油，財政困局因此緩和，一九三六年成立的國營石油機構即以此為基礎；巴拉圭則確保了河運與大片牧場與白木林的經濟價值。兩國大批退伍軍人成為日後軍事與政治決策的核心，查科經驗也深刻影響了拉美此後的將軍政治。
impactEn: The war was among the bloodiest conflicts of twentieth-century South America, and it also carried the full modern form of war into a tropical interior: heavy machine guns, light tanks, towed guns, mortars and air forces all committed to mass destruction, making it the first war in the Americas to use modern weapons on a large scale and the first large-scale air war. Its technical legacy is the most durable, for aerial supply, encirclement guided by aerial reconnaissance, mobility sustained by roads and narrow-gauge railways, and a defensive system of wooden stockades with interlocking fields of fire were all tested here and later borrowed by the European wars. The intervention of Britain, the United States and Italy through observers, advisers and engineering expertise also set a precedent for great powers to shape a regional conflict without formally entering it. Politically, Bolivia had already seen an armed revolt before the war, and the army's operations in the Chaco against the insurgents went beyond its orders, damaging both morale and public opinion; after the war the reformist current overthrew the long-dominant oligarchy, and the military's political weight rose accordingly, until the officers seized power outright a few years later. Paraguay, for its part, used the victory to entrench an authoritarian system: Estigarribia went on to serve as president, pursued national reform, and was assassinated in 1940. In the long run the Chaco remained an unarbitrated vacuum between the two world wars, and only the final treaty of 1938 fixed the permanent frontier. Economically, Bolivia at last found and began producing oil in the Chaco, easing its fiscal distress, and the state oil organisation founded in 1936 grew out of that discovery; Paraguay in turn secured navigation rights and the economic value of its vast pastures and quebracho forests. Large numbers of demobilised men became the core of military and political decision-making in both countries, and the Chaco experience coloured the military politics of Latin America for decades.
result: 勝負由後勤而非火力決定。一九三二年至三三年，巴拉圭以鐵路為骨幹的攻勢把戰線推過布克耶隆，玻利維亞一九三二年底至三三年初的北向反攻一度奪回科拉萊斯並打到納納瓦外圍，卻因缺乏補給支撐而無法擴大成果；一九三四年五月起巴拉圭反攻，十二月更深入玻利維亞境內二百餘公里、攻陷皮賴，一度直逼聖克魯斯；一九三五年三至四月玻利維亞集中兵力反攻，在亞帕卡尼一線擊潰巴拉圭前衛，把戰線推回舊界一帶。雙方都已被消耗殆盡，後勤崩潰、士氣低落，疾病與麻痺困擾前線，一九三五年六月十四日停戰生效，六月十七日在布宜諾斯艾利斯簽訂和約與邊界協議，一九三八年召開查科和平會議追認永久邊界，劃分一直延續至今。協議大體以實際控制線為基礎：玻利維亞保住它在戰爭中實據的北部查科地帶與油田，巴拉圭保有廣大查科的其餘部分，並取得上巴拉圭河航運權與若干沿河據點；以整個查科計，巴拉圭保住了約四分之三的面積。對玻利維亞而言這是一場代價慘重而收益有限的敗仗，卻換來了石油資源與一條通海出口走廊長期爭取的資本；對巴拉圭而言這是一場立國之戰，確立了它在南美洲中部的小強國地位，同時留下軍人干政的傳統，而退役軍人的政治影響力，此後數十年在兩國都不斷發酵。
resultEn: The outcome was decided by logistics rather than by firepower. In 1932 and 1933 the Paraguayan offensive, built on its railway network, pushed the front past Boquerón; a Bolivian counter-offensive from the north at the end of 1932 and in early 1933 retook Corrales and reached the outskirts of Nanawa, but could not be enlarged for want of supply, and from May 1934 Paraguay counter-attacked, driving more than 200 kilometres into Bolivian territory in December and taking Piraí in a thrust that brought it within sight of Santa Cruz. In March and April 1935 Bolivia concentrated its forces for a counter-offensive, destroyed the Paraguayan vanguard along the Yapacaní and pushed the front back towards the old line. Both armies were exhausted, their logistics broken, their morale low, with disease and dysentery afflicting the front, and on 14 June 1935 the ceasefire took effect; the peace and boundary agreement was signed in Buenos Aires on 17 June, and the Chaco Peace Conference of 1938 ratified the permanent frontier, which has lasted ever since. The agreement broadly followed the lines actually held: Bolivia kept the northern strip of the Chaco it had occupied in the fighting together with the oil, while Paraguay retained the rest of the vast Chaco, gained navigation rights on the upper Paraguay River and a number of river outposts; measured against the whole Chaco, Paraguay kept about three quarters of the area. For Bolivia this was a ruinous war that bought little, yet it left the country oil and the capital of a long campaign for an outlet to the sea. For Paraguay it was a war of national foundation, fixing its position as a small but assertive power in central South America, while leaving behind the tradition of military politics, and the political pull of the demobilised men kept working in both countries for decades afterwards.
